name: Dimapur Town
description: Largest city and commercial gateway of Nagaland, located on the Dhansiri River plains, serving as the primary entry point by air and rail for the state.
facts: Main airport and railway hub of Nagaland
Elevation around 145 m
Ancient capital of the Kachari kingdom

name: Kachari Ruins
description: Medieval ruins of the Kachari Rajbari featuring distinctive mushroom-domed sandstone pillars and carved monoliths from the 10th-13th century Dimasa Kachari kingdom.
facts: Protected by Archaeological Survey of India
Mushroom-shaped pillars believed to be fertility symbols or chess pieces
Best visited October to March

name: Green Park
description: Landscaped recreational park inside the State Horticulture Nursery at 4th Mile, featuring greenery, boating, ziplining, and picnic facilities popular with families.
facts: Located within State Horticulture Nursery
Offers boating, water zorbing and ziplining
Ideal for picnics in winter months

name: NEZCC Stone Garden and Museum
description: North East Zone Cultural Centre complex with a stone sculpture garden of 31 artworks by Indian sculptors and a heritage museum showcasing crafts from eight northeastern states.
facts: Located near Dimapur Airport and railway station
Features traditional morungs and amphitheatre
Preserves Northeast cultural artifacts

name: Niathu Resort
description: 50-acre resort near Dimapur Airport meaning 'Sunrise' in Angami, offering alpine-style chalets, anthurium gardens and family amenities by the Chate River.
facts: Five-minute drive from Dimapur Airport
Seven alpine chalet suites
Popular for short getaways

name: Noune Resort
description: Peaceful mini-tourist resort at Seithekiema A village about 10 km from Dimapur, featuring a large water body for boating and angling plus children's facilities.
facts: Name means Peace in Angami Naga
Offers water zorbing and adventure activities
Pastoral setting ideal for relaxation

name: Heirloom Naga Centre
description: Creative hub near Sovima Village uniting Naga craft brands, workshops, gallery and guest house showcasing traditional and contemporary Naga design.
facts: Approximately 15 minutes from Dimapur Airport
Features Heirloom gallery of curated Naga artifacts
Supports local artisans through retail and mentorship

name: Hong Kong Market
description: Bustling flea market in central Dimapur known for imported goods, clothing, electronics and local Naga products, a vibrant commercial landmark.
facts: One of the most popular markets in Dimapur
Mix of local handicrafts and imported items
Lively street food nearby

name: Kohima Town
description: Capital of Nagaland and major hill station perched on ridges at around 1,444 m elevation, known for its scenic views, Angami Naga culture, and role as the state's administrative and cultural hub.
facts: Capital city of Nagaland
Elevation approximately 1,444 metres
Site of the decisive 1944 Battle of Kohima

name: Kohima War Cemetery
description: Commonwealth War Graves Commission cemetery on Garrison Hill commemorating soldiers who died in the Battle of Kohima in April 1944, featuring the famous tennis court lines and the epitaph 'When you go home tell them of us and say for your tomorrow we gave our today'.
facts: Contains 1,420 Commonwealth burials from WWII
Marks the site of the Battle of Kohima that halted Japanese advance into India
Maintained by the Commonwealth War Graves Commission

name: Kisama Heritage Village
description: Open-air Naga Heritage Village located between Kigwema and Phesama, designed as a traditional Naga settlement with morungs of all major tribes, and the permanent venue of the annual Hornbill Festival.
facts: Permanent venue of the Hornbill Festival held every December
Name derived from neighbouring villages Kigwema and Phesama
About 12 km south of Kohima on NH-2

name: Khonoma Green Village
description: Western Angami Naga village 20 km west of Kohima, recognised as India's first Green Village for its community-led conservation, terraced paddy fields, and the Khonoma Nature Conservation and Tragopan Sanctuary protecting Blyth's Tragopan.
facts: India's first Green Village with community conservation since 1990s
Home to the endangered Blyth's Tragopan
Historic site of resistance against British colonial forces

name: Dzukou Valley
description: High-altitude valley of rolling meadows and dwarf bamboo at about 2,450 m on the Kohima (Nagaland)–Senapati (Manipur) border, famous for seasonal wildflowers including the rare Dzukou lily and popular for moderate treks.
facts: Straddles Nagaland–Manipur border; most approaches from Viswema or Jakhama
Elevation around 2,438–2,452 metres
Best visited October to March for clear weather and blooms

name: Japfu Peak
description: Second-highest peak in Nagaland at 3,048 m in the Barail Range, about 15 km south of Kohima, known for trekking trails, panoramic views, and the world's tallest rhododendron tree.
facts: Elevation 3,048 metres; second highest in Nagaland after Saramati
Holds Guinness record for tallest rhododendron tree (~20 m)
Trek usually starts from Kigwema village; receives occasional winter snow

name: Nagaland State Museum
description: Ethnographic museum on Bayavü Hill in Kohima displaying artefacts, traditional dresses, weapons, musical instruments, and cultural items from all Naga tribes, established in 1970.
facts: Opened to public on 25 November 1970
Operated by Department of Art and Culture, Nagaland
Comprehensive collection covering Naga tribal material culture

name: Mary Help of Christians Cathedral
description: Cathedral of the Diocese of Kohima, notable for architecture that incorporates traditional Naga house elements and a large carved wooden crucifix; consecrated in 1991.
facts: Consecrated in January 1991
Features a 16-foot carved wooden crucifix
Partly funded as a memorial related to the Battle of Kohima

name: Dzüleke Village
description: Small Angami Naga village in Kohima district focused on eco-tourism, with community conservation, homestays, streams, and access toward Dzukou Valley area; known for quiet nature and terraced fields.
facts: Population around 156 (2011); community-led eco-tourism since late 1990s
Approximately 30–40 km from Kohima
Ideal for slow travel and nature walks

name: Touphema Tourist Village
description: Community-based tourist village about 36–41 km from Kohima recreating a traditional Angami Naga settlement with thatched huts, cultural performances, local cuisine, and panoramic valley views.
facts: About 36–41 km from Kohima on the road toward Wokha
Model of community-based tourism with traditional cottages
Offers cultural dances, local food, and museum exhibits

name: Mon Town
description: District headquarters of Mon and gateway to the Konyak Naga heartland, a small hill town at around 655 m elevation serving as the base for exploring nearby villages, culture and nature.
facts: Headquarters of Mon district, home of the Konyak Nagas
Elevation approximately 655 metres
Base for visits to Longwa, Shangnyu and other cultural villages

name: Longwa Village
description: Large Konyak Naga village straddling the India–Myanmar international border in Mon district; the hereditary Angh’s (chief’s) house sits directly on the border line, and residents hold dual citizenship under the Free Movement Regime.
facts: Angh’s house is bisected by the India–Myanmar border
Known for traditional Konyak culture and remaining tattooed elders
About 35–45 km from Mon town; best October–April

name: Shangnyu Village
description: Prominent Konyak village near Mon featuring a 500-year-old Angh’s house, an 8-foot wooden monument with carvings of humans and animals believed to be of ancient origin, and memorial stones.
facts: Angh’s house and wooden monument are main attractions
Approximately 6–18 km from Mon town
Showcases traditional Konyak woodcraft and history

name: Chui Village
description: Traditional Konyak village close to Mon town known for its wooden architecture, morungs, Angh’s house and displays of cultural artefacts including skull trophies from the historical headhunting period.
facts: About 5–8 km from Mon town; easily accessible
Features traditional wooden houses and cultural displays
Good introduction to Konyak village life

name: Chi Village
description: One of the oldest villages in Nagaland, located near Mon town, ruled by an Angh and known for its morungs with wood sculptures, log drums and historical displays of skulls from the headhunting era.
facts: Approximately 7 km from Mon town
One of the oldest settlements in the region
Displays traditional Konyak artefacts and sculptures

name: Singphan Wildlife Sanctuary
description: 23.57 km² wildlife sanctuary in Mon district along the Assam border, notified in 2009 and declared Singphan Elephant Reserve in 2018; important corridor for Asian elephants and home to wet evergreen and moist deciduous forests.
facts: Notified as wildlife sanctuary in 2009; Elephant Reserve in 2018
Area approximately 23.57 square kilometres
Supports Asian elephant movement between Nagaland and Assam

name: Naginimora
description: Subdivision town in western Mon district on the Dikhu River, serving as a trading and gateway point near the Assam border with historical coal mining links and weekly markets blending Konyak and Assamese cultures.
facts: Subdivision headquarters in Mon district
Located on the bank of the Dikhu River
Historical coalfield area near Kongan and Borjan

name: Veda Peak
description: Highest peak in Mon district (locally Pak Koi), about 70 km east of Mon town, offering panoramic views of the Brahmaputra and Chindwin river systems on clear days, with a nearby waterfall; popular for moderate treks.
facts: Highest point in Mon district
Approximately 70 km from Mon town
Views of Brahmaputra (India) and Chindwin (Myanmar) on clear days; nearby waterfall

name: Chenloisho Village
description: Large Konyak village in the Chen area of Mon district near the India–Myanmar border, known for its small museum of traditional ornaments and cultural artefacts.
facts: Located in Chen circle, near the international border
Features a small museum of traditional Konyak ornaments
One of the larger villages in the Chen area
